STATUS: DEVELOPMENT-ONLY -- official protocol, development seeds; official sets remain sealed

VERDICT.headline: UNDERPOWERED BY CONSTRUCTION. Both arms found ZERO actives on all three seeds, which is exactly the expected outcome, so the test cannot discriminate between exploration and the control.

base_rate_correction.measured_over: 80,000 random ZINC molecules from banked random-zinc runs
base_rate_correction.correction: the true rate at jnk3>=0.3 is 0.040%, roughly 50x lower than the premise. The ~2% figure describes the ENRICHED pools from earlier GA and adaptive runs, not a random-120 start.

the_decisive_check.question: did 180 search calls improve on the initial 120 at all?
the_decisive_check.reading: on two of three seeds NEITHER arm improved on its own starting population by any amount. The budget, not the policy, is the binding constraint.

budget_required_for_power.note: 7,500 draws is most of the 10,000-call benchmark budget, so 'find an active from random-120' is not a tiny-charged-test question when the metric is a binary activity threshold.

VERDICT.what_is_NOT_concluded: nothing about whether exploration beats fixed scalarization at discovery. The test had no power to tell, and the offline smoke showed the policies do behave completely differently (100% divergence, 98% vs 22% start-repeat).
VERDICT.incidental_durability_result: one container was preempted mid-run and Modal retried it. The replacement RESUMED from the ledger and completed correctly: 300 records, 300 distinct, contiguous sequence 0-299. Per-container counters like `expansions` undercount across a retry (8 reported against 19+ observed before preemption), which is a reporting artifact and not an accounting one -- the charged count and the ledger are correct.
